summary: Genuinely mutual NDA on CloudVantage paper that largely matches the playbook, with a narrowed evidence standard for the carve-outs and an uncovered breach-notification duty.

findings.quote: disclosed by or on behalf of a Party or its Affiliates (the "Disclosing Party") to the other Party or its Affiliates (the "Receiving Party")
findings.why: Disclosing and Receiving Party are defined so either party can be either, and the obligations in clause 2 apply equally to both.

findings.quote: designated as "Confidential," "Proprietary," or with a similar legend at the time of disclosure, or that reasonably should be understood to be confidential
findings.why: Covers marked information or information reasonably understood to be confidential, and includes notes and analyses derived from it.

findings.quote: solely as necessary to evaluate, pursue, or fulfill the Purpose and for no other purpose whatsoever
findings.why: Use is limited to the Purpose, which is a potential commercial relationship between the parties.

findings.quote: that the Receiving Party can prove by competent, contemporaneous written evidence
findings.why: All four carve-outs are present, but they must be proved by contemporaneous written evidence, which is narrower than the accepted 'written records' or 'reasonable evidence' standard.
findings.draft_redline: that the Receiving Party can demonstrate by reasonable evidence or written records:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are happy with the four exclusions, but ask that the evidence standard be reasonable evidence or written records rather than contemporaneous written evidence, as the latter may be hard to meet in practice for either of us.

findings.quote: may disclose such Confidential Information to those of its Representatives who have a bona fide need to know such information for the Purpose
findings.why: Disclosure is allowed on a need-to-know basis to directors, officers, employees, advisers, accountants and insurers of the party and its Affiliates, with the recipient liable for them under 2.3.3.

findings.quote: the Receiving Party may make such disclosure to the minimum extent legally required, provided that the Receiving Party shall, to the extent legally permissible:
findings.why: Disclosure is permitted where required by law, regulator, court or stock exchange; notice is only to the extent legally permissible and cooperation is at the Disclosing Party's expense.

findings.quote: within ten (10) business days either promptly return to the Disclosing Party all tangible materials embodying the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information or permanently destroy and erase all such materials
findings.why: 10 business day period with a backup and legal-retention exception in 5.2 (retained copies stay confidential); certification is by an authorised representative rather than an officer.
findings.fallback_cited: Confirmation by email from an authorised person rather than an officer.

findings.quote: shall remain the sole and exclusive property of the Disclosing Party or its licensors. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as granting any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, or other intellectual property right or license
findings.why: Confidential Information and IP stay with the Disclosing Party and no licence is granted beyond use for the Purpose.

findings.quote: ALL CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION IS PROVIDED "AS IS" WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY OF ANY KIND. NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY REPRESENTATIONS OR WARRANTIES
findings.why: Mutual as-is disclaimer with no warranty, and 6.3 confirms no obligation to proceed; there is no liability exclusion that removes a fraud carve-out.

findings.quote: Neither Party shall issue any press release or make any public announcement regarding the existence of this Agreement or the discussions between the Parties
findings.why: Mutual restriction on announcements without prior written consent.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years thereafter, unless terminated earlier by either Party upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: Two-year term with 30 days' notice to terminate early, as preferred.

findings.quote: shall survive for a fixed period of thirty-six (36) months following the effective date of such expiration or termination
findings.why: Survival of 3 years with trade secrets protected for as long as they remain trade secrets, as preferred.

findings.quote: the Disclosing Party shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief, specific performance, and other equitable remedies from any court of competent jurisdiction, in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity, without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting any bond or other security
findings.why: Equitable relief is available to the Disclosing Party (so to either party), remedies are cumulative, and the wording is 'entitled to seek' with no bond.
findings.fallback_cited: 'Entitled to seek' rather than 'entitled to'; no requirement to post a bond.

findings.quote: governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of England and Wales
findings.why: English law with exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales, as preferred.

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign or transfer this Agreement, or any of its rights or obligations hereunder, without the prior written consent of the other Party
findings.why: Mutual no-assignment without prior written consent.

findings.quote: shall not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, translate, or otherwise attempt to derive the source code
findings.why: Prohibits reverse engineering of software and prototypes, as preferred.

findings.quote: shall promptly notify the Disclosing Party in writing upon discovering any actual or suspected unauthorized use, loss, or disclosure of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information
findings.why: A mutual duty to notify of suspected unauthorised use or loss and to cooperate is not covered by any playbook rule, so it needs lawyer review.
